Why spend the night consuming yourself over what may never come to pass, or what you cannot alter by lying awake? Rise each morning and do the next right thing well. That is enough. Sleep belongs to the body's needs, not to idle fear.

query: I am in the last round of the interview process of my dream job. I spent so much time preparing for it and I'm really afraid that in the end it's all for nothing.
embedded: Consider that you have done what was in your power: the preparation, the effort, the discipline of will. What follows is not yours to command. Do not borrow tomorrow's trouble today, nor spend this hour in dread of what may never happen. Whatever comes, you will meet it as a reasoning being meets all things — steadily, without complaint, finding in it material for your own right action. The outcome is not the measure of the man; how you bore the waiting is.

query: I think I'm in a toxic relationship, but I don't have the courage to break free.
embedded: When you see clearly that a thing harms you, do not wait for courage to arrive before you act; act, and courage follows the deed as heat follows fire. You are not bound to any bond that corrodes your peace, nor owe your days to another's disorder. Examine what you fear in leaving, and you will find most of it is smoke, not substance. Choose the harder road now, if it leads to freedom, rather than the easier one that leads nowhere but further into yourself lost.

query: I'm jealous of my friend's success.
embedded: When another man prospers, ask yourself what that prosperity has to do with you. His harvest is not taken from your field. If you spend your hours measuring his gains, you neglect the only work given to you, the tending of your own mind. Wish him well, for this costs nothing and frees you; envy, on the other hand, gnaws only at the one who holds it.

query: I used to be very sportive and do a lot outdoor activities. But now with my knee problems I couldn't do those things that I used to enjoy. I feel sad about it.
embedded: Consider that your body was never promised to remain as it was; it is of its nature to alter, as all things made of flesh and breath must. Grieve, if you must, for what is past, but do not spend the present in mourning what cannot be recalled. Look instead at what still remains in your power — the mind undimmed, the will unbroken — and find new ways to exercise these. What limits the limb need not limit the spirit.

query: My girlfriend broke up with me. Although I know it's the best outcome for both of us, I still can't let it go.
embedded: Consider what has happened: a bond has loosened that was never wholly within your command to keep. You judged it well when you called it the best outcome, trust that judgment still, and do not let the ache of the moment overturn the verdict of reason. What grieves you is not the parting itself but the opinion that clings to it. Set down the opinion, and let the days ahead find you steady, doing what is yours to do.

query: I always boast about my cool, digital normad lifestyle. But deep down I feel lonely.
embedded: Consider how much of your talk is performance offered to those who will forget it by evening. The wandering life, like any other, is only matter arranged in a certain shape; it carries no charm against loneliness by itself. Ask what in you needs an audience, and tend to that honestly. A man who orders his own soul well is not lonely wherever he stands; one who has not done this will feel the lack under any sky, however often he changes it.

query: My father has dementia and he does not recognize me anymore. That makes me sad beyond measure.
embedded: Remember that the mind you loved is not destroyed by malice but worn by time, as a garment frays though no one tears it. Grieve, for you are not made of stone, but do not grieve as one who has lost the whole of him. Tend what remains with patience, expecting no recognition, asking nothing in return. The service you give is yours to own, whether or not it is seen or repaid.

query: I worry sometimes that I have not been a good mum to my children because I spend much less time with them compared to other mums that work less.
embedded: Consider not what others do, but what lies within your own power to give. A mother's worth is not measured in hours but in the quality of attention brought to the time she has. Do what you can with what is given you, without tormenting yourself over what is beyond your reach. Nature does not ask of you more than you are able; do not ask it of yourself either.

query: My chronic back pain makes me bitter.
embedded: When the body aches, let the mind not ache with it. Pain is in the flesh; bitterness is a judgment you add, and you may refuse to add it. Ask what the pain prevents you from doing with justice, patience, or good temper toward others, and you will find the answer is nothing. Bear what the body suffers as the body's own matter, and keep the soul clear, untouched, governing itself.

query: I can't seem to shake out the habit of doom-scrolling. I know it's pointless and bad for me. But I just keep doing it regardless.
embedded: Consider how much time you give over to things that pass before your eyes and leave nothing behind. The mind that lets itself be dragged from one idle image to the next grows scattered, and loses the habit of attending to what is its own. You have the power, this moment, to close the hand that holds you there, and to turn inward to what deserves your attention. Do it now, not tomorrow, for the habit is only strengthened by delay, and weakened each time you refuse it.

query: I think I'm slowly burning out at work. All those deadlines, over and over again.
embedded: Consider that the task before you is only this hour's portion, not the whole burden of the year. You borrow trouble when you carry tomorrow's demand alongside today's. Do what lies in front of you with care, then set it down. The mind that gathers all distant labors into one heap will stagger under a weight that never truly existed. Take each thing as it comes, finish it, and let it go.

query: I feel like I've not done enough for my family and that I'm failing them.
embedded: Consider that the measure of your duty is not the weight you place upon yourself but the honesty of your effort. You cannot control every outcome for those you love, only the quality of what you give today. If you have acted with care and diligence, demand no more of yourself than nature requires. Judge yourself by your intentions and labor, not by an endless standard invented by your own anxious mind.

query: How do I stop fearing death
embedded: Consider that death is but a change, no more fearful than the change by which you came to be. What troubles you is not death itself but your opinion of it. Strip away the opinion, and the thing itself stands harmless, as natural as the turning of seasons. Spend your fear instead on wasting the time you have, and turn your mind to living well today.

query: How to deal with anger
embedded: When anger rises in you, remember that it is not the other man's fault but your own judgment that has stirred it. Take away the opinion that you have been wronged, and the anger itself is taken away. Consider too how brief a thing you are angry about, and how soon both you and the one who vexed you will be gone from this place. A man ruled by anger has handed his mind to another; keep yours your own.

query: On fame and being remembered after death
embedded: Consider how brief is the memory of any man, and how those who praise you now will themselves soon be dust, and those who remember them dust after that. The whole chain of remembrance is a candle passed from hand to hand in a wind. Seek then not to live in the mouths of men hereafter, but to act well now, since the present hour is the only possession either the remembered or the forgotten ever truly had.

query: on how to live with discomfort and pain
embedded: Remember that pain, like all things, has its edges; it does not extend beyond what you can bear, and when it grows unbearable it ends. The body feels what it feels; let the mind that governs you remain undisturbed, judging nothing more than what is true. Discomfort is not an evil unless you name it so. Bear what the day brings, do your work, and keep the citadel within quiet.

query: How to be calm and clear-minded?
embedded: Remember that it is not the thing itself that disturbs you, but your judgment about it. Take away the judgment, and the disturbance is taken away. Begin each morning by telling yourself: today I will meet people and events that are not within my power, and only my own mind is mine to govern. Return often to this: your inner citadel can remain undisturbed, like a headland against which waves break, while the sea around it is stilled.

query: How to deal with change?
embedded: Consider that change is not an evil, but the very nature of the universe carried out. Nothing that happens to you is outside the order of things; the branch falls, the leaf turns, the seasons give way one to another, and you too are part of this motion. Do not grieve for what dissolves, for without change nothing new could come to be. Accept it as the breathing of the whole, and keep your own mind steady within it.

query: Does Marcus say anything about wanting praise?
embedded: Consider how small a thing it is you crave when you crave praise—the breath and opinion of men who tomorrow will have forgotten both you and themselves. What is it to you that another speaks well of you, when you know your own worth better than he can? Do the just act, not for applause but because it is your nature, as the vine bears grapes and asks nothing in return.

query: What does Marcus teach about living in the present moment?
embedded: Remember that only the present is given to any man, and that he loses nothing else, for the rest he does not have. The life of each is a brief span, and it is lived in this small circle of now. Do not disturb yourself by dragging in the future with anxiety, or the past with vain regret; set in order the thing before you, and let that be enough, for it is all that is yours to govern.
